title: Noether: a conservation law for cross-chain value, enforced by Reactive

scenes.say: Bridge hacks have cost users well over a billion dollars: Ronin, Wormhole, Nomad, Multichain. Each time, every chain saw a valid transaction. No single chain could see that the books didn't balance.

Noether is that missing view. It's a reactive contract on Reactive Network that enforces one law across chains: every token delivered on one chain must have been dispatched, exactly once, on the other. It subscribes to Hyperlane on Base and Unichain, keeps the ledger inside react, and if the law breaks, its callbacks freeze the route everywhere. No bot, no server, no keeper.

Let's run it live, on testnet. First, an honest transfer: a thousand dollars locked on Base, and delivered on Unichain by Hyperlane. Noether matches it to its dispatch by message ID, and stays silent.

Now the attack. With a stolen relayer key, I forge a message that mints a million tokens with nothing behind them, and Hyperlane's real Mailbox accepts it. Within seconds, Noether's ledger flips to breached: its neural scorer, running inside react, rated the delivery a forgery.

The dossier rebuilds it from on-chain timestamps: Noether decided in zero seconds, and one reaction landed four callbacks, freezing Base and Unichain, closing cover sales, and quarantining the attacker. The attacker tries again, and the frozen route rejects it.

Here's what Reactive gives Noether. The system contract, for subscriptions and callbacks. Subscriptions made inside react: a cron clock that only runs while something looks suspicious, and taint tracing on the attacker. One reaction, four callbacks, two chains. All for about one and a half hundredths of a REACT per reaction.
And you don't rebuild your bridge to use it. Monitor mode audits any Hyperlane route with zero integration. Enforce mode wraps an existing route in one command, in about two minutes.
Five live runs, forty-four tests, every transaction linked. Noether. Every second counts. Every unit is accounted for.
